# Jam-a-Lot User Manual

Welcome to **Jam-a-Lot**, your browser-based jazz practice companion. Jam-a-Lot plays synthesized acoustic drums, double bass, and electric piano accompaniment over a jazz standard's chord changes while displaying a clean lead-sheet style chart. 

---

Bossa, Salsa and Bolero fills use brief cross-stick/timbale cues, eighth-note chorus pickups, and spaced cadenza endings instead of rapid rolls. Bolero uses two-stroke cues without doubles, and its section arrival replaces the existing timbale hit.

The Chord Editor’s Time signature selector includes 2/4 in text and grid modes. Text mode updates `Time:`; Save Changes applies it. Grid edits preserve chord proportions and explicit one-bar meter overrides. Import previews show the meter. Bossa Nova fits its full accompaniment and final pickup into each two-beat bar at the displayed quarter-note BPM; a punch at `2.5` means & of 2.

### Practice Video — slow down and repeat a phrase

Open **Song Info → Play Video**. In Song Resources, press **Play** on a saved or discovered YouTube version to open the same controls; saved links stay unloaded until you open them. Song Info opens the saved video or canonical recording for the current tune; for an unlinked original, attach a YouTube link in the inline bar. Press **Play video** or the video's own Play button to begin.

- **Speed**: choose a slower or faster rate from those reported by this video. **1× · Original** restores normal speed. The displayed selection follows YouTube's confirmed rate. YouTube provides pitch-preserving slowdown; audio quality at very slow speeds depends on its player and your browser.
- **−5s / +5s**: replay or skip five seconds. These buttons turn phrase looping off so you can find another passage.
- **Set A / Set B**: mark the current position as the phrase start/end. B must be at least half a second after A. Moving A beyond B clears B. Marker times show tenths of a second.
- **Loop A–B**: toggle phrase repetition; enabling it jumps to A. Press Play if paused. **Go to A** returns to the marked start. **Clear A/B** removes both markers.
- **Calculate BPM**: expand the calculator. While the video plays, press **Tap beat** on each quarter note at least four times. It uses recent taps and restarts after a pause, speed change, or a gap longer than three seconds (extended at slow playback rates). **Reset taps** starts over. For a counted measurement, mark **A** on a beat and **B** after a known number of beats, enter **Quarter-note beats A–B**, then press **Calculate from A/B**. Four bars of 4/4 = 16 beats; four bars of 3/4 = 12; each dotted-quarter pulse in 6/8 = 1.5 quarter-note beats. Count intervals: B is the beat immediately after the counted span. Longer spans reduce marker error. Results show the original recording's quarter-note BPM and the effective BPM at the confirmed playback speed. This is manual measurement, not automatic audio analysis; it does not change the band's tempo. Tap results are temporary, while saved A/B markers can be reused.
- Markers and the last confirmed speed are saved **on this device, separately for each song and video**. Reopening restores them with looping off; it does not start playback automatically. Blocked browser storage leaves the controls usable for the current visit.
- Starting a video pauses the band and other practice videos. Starting/resuming the band pauses videos. Closing Song Info or changing tunes releases its players.
- YouTube controls availability, ads, and supported rates; phrase loops may have a short gap. If a recording cannot play in the embed, use **Open on YouTube ↗** or attach another version. Spotify keeps its provider player and does not gain these video controls.


### Solo Transcription — private improvisation drafts

Open **Toolbox → Solo Transcription**, or **Solo Transcription · local recording** beside a Practice Video. The video shortcut copies its A/B timestamps into **From / To**; use them only if your local file matches that video's timing. The panel is one window: a header, one toolbar, the score and a slim footer. **⤢ Full screen** (header) enlarges it to the whole browser window; press it again to return.

1. **New transcription** (microphone icon; open automatically when the tune has no draft): **Choose recording…** — an original recording, or an authorized file from the performer/rights holder. It stays in the browser. Sources up to **75 MB / 15 minutes**; WAV, MP3 or M4A are the most reliable. Set **From / To** (seconds) to a **2–180 second (up to three minutes)** passage — the limit turns red when the span is out of range — and **Range** to the concert-pitch window (default C3–C7). Press **Transcribe**; a progress bar and **Cancel** appear. Closing the panel or changing tune also cancels. A failed or cancelled run keeps the existing draft. **Rights** expands the note on authorized sources; audio is never extracted from YouTube.
2. **Transport** (toolbar, left): **Play / Pause** (or **Space**) and **⏮ Back to start**, with the position clock. **Notes · Original · Both** chooses what plays: the transcribed pitches, the original recording over the same span, or both together to check the transcription against the record. Original and Both need the exact source file; after reopening a saved draft, clicking either asks for it. Clicking a note moves the play position to it, so Play starts there; a dashed line marks a paused position. While playing, a vertical cursor follows the audio, **orange** notes are sounding and **blue** have played, and the score scrolls to keep the cursor in view. Starting the band or a practice video stops it.
3. **Edit tools** (toolbar, middle): **Select** (click a note; drag it up/down to change pitch; ↑/↓ moves a semitone, Shift an octave — a melody note taken under middle C moves to the bass staff; ⌥↑ / ⌥↓ move a note between the staves without changing its pitch; Delete/Backspace removes it), **Add** (click the staff to place a note from the key signature; pick the new note length — sixteenth, eighth, quarter, half — beside the tools), **Erase** (click notes to remove them) and **Pan** (drag the page). **Add** places the note on the staff you click. **Undo / Redo** (⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z) keep 50 steps. The footer shows the selected note's name with pitch ▲/▼, **Start** and **Length** in seconds, **Bass staff / Treble staff** (moves the note to the other staff) and a delete button; otherwise it shows the note count and the last status message.
4. **Grand staff.** The score is piano sheet music: the title, *Solo transcription*, the composer and the tempo head the page; a brace and barlines join a treble staff and a bass (F clef) staff. The **treble staff is one voice** — the melody line, each note ending where the next begins — and **everything else goes on the bass staff**. The line is picked by a path that may skip an attack, so left-hand or bass attacks between melody notes go below; a high note the path passed over joins the melody when nothing else is sounding, and takes over an attack it shares with a lower melody note. Where the left hand plays high, the bass staff switches to treble clef for those bars (a small clef marks each change) instead of stacking ledger lines. Weaker octave/twelfth ghosts of a louder note (a known Basic Pitch artifact) are removed once after transcription and counted in the status line. The split is stored with each note: **Bass staff / Treble staff** in the footer (or ⌥↓ / ⌥↑) fixes one note, and **Re-split staves** (toolbar) redoes the whole split — undoable. There is no instrument separation, so with a band the bass staff includes the bassist (and any guitar); a solo-piano recording or a piano stem gives the left hand alone.
5. **Chords between the staves.** When the tune has a chart, its solo-form chords are written between the staves, with boxed rehearsal marks (**A**, **B**…) where each section starts. With no sync points the passage is aligned automatically to the chart bar whose harmony best matches the bass staff (ties go to the top of the form). To sync, **click the chord area of any bar**: choose the section that starts there (**A · 1**, **A · 9**, **B · 17**…) or the exact chart bar. Each sync point holds until the next one, so if the player stretches or skips a bar, add another sync point where the next section begins; synced bars show a filled rehearsal mark. **Remove** deletes a sync point and **Auto** returns to automatic alignment. Chords also follow the notation tempo, so set ♩= to the recording first. Sync points are saved with the draft.
6. **Notation** (toolbar, right): **♩=** sets the notation tempo and the meter menu the time signature. A new transcription starts at the **recording's** tempo, detected from the note attacks and the chart (the status line shows *♩=… detected*); the tune's practice tempo is only the fallback, since records are often played at double or half of it. **Detect** re-runs the detection on the current notes, and **½× / 2×** halve or double the tempo — use them when every score bar holds two chart bars (or half of one). Changing the tempo with these buttons clears the chart sync points, because they name score bars that have moved. Passage start is beat one; rhythm is rounded to sixteenths for display only — stored seconds and playback never change. A transcription records attacks well and releases poorly, so a rest shorter than a beat between two notes on the same staff is shown as the first note held (tied where it crosses a beat or barline) instead of isolated sixteenths and rests; longer rests stay. Every line holds at least two bars. Clefs, key signatures and accidentals are drawn at printed size; at 100% zoom the notes sit slightly smaller than the text. Notes are spelled in the tune's key; both key signatures repeat on every system with standard accidental rules, beams within beats (dotted quarters in 6/8) and ties for held notes. The whole passage is one continuous score whose systems reflow to the window width: **− / +** zoom (50–200%; click the percentage to reset), and zooming out — especially in full screen — fits more bars on each line to see the whole solo at once.
7. **Save** (⌘S) stores the notes and notation settings as one private draft per tune in this browser, replacing the previous one; the button reads **Saved** when nothing has changed. Reopening Solo Transcription, or **Melody Staff → Open saved solo study**, restores it without rerunning inference. Header icons: **Open study file**; **Download** → **Sheet music (PDF)** (letter-size pages with the title block, both staves, chords, rehearsal marks and page numbers, laid out at a fixed print width whatever the screen zoom) or **Study file (JSON)**, a private `<tune>-solo-study.json` (no audio) that **Open study file** restores for the same tune — press Save afterwards to keep an opened file; and **Delete draft** removes the browser copy after a confirmation. Closing without saving loses new work. There is no MIDI/MusicXML export and pitch bends are not reproduced.

Improvised solo studies work on standards, imported tunes and originals. They stay out of tune melodies, cloud sync, sharing and the public catalog. **Melody Staff** edits composed melodies for originals and **Staff** shows the generated band; both share the solo score's note renderer, key-signature glyphs and accidental rules. **Melody Staff → Open saved solo study** opens this private editor; it does not import notes into the composed melody, and solo-study JSON is not interchangeable with Melody Staff's MusicXML.

## 1. Playback & Live Performance Controls

### Transport Controls
Located at the top of the interface:
- **Play / Stop / Pause**: Controls the playback state.
- **Count-in**: Select between 1 or 2 bars of count-in.
- **Metronome**: Toggle a metronome click on or off.
- **User Menu**: Sign in via Google OAuth or Email/Password, manage cloud library sync, give feedback via the Feedback modal, and view active user preferences.

### User Account & Preferences Menu
Located on the far right of the top navigation bar:
- **Join Beta Program / Account Button**: Labeled **"Join Beta Program"** (with sparkles icon) when signed out to encourage joining the free Beta program. Toggles the user profile menu when signed in.
- **Guest Mode Notice Banner**: Displays a persistent top notification for unauthenticated users explaining Guest Mode capabilities (access to 3 demo tunes: *Blues in F*, *Oleo*, & *Mr. P.C.*) and inviting users to join the free Beta Program.
- **Guest Restrictions**: Guests can play the 3 demo songs with full generated audio. All other catalog tunes (1,000+ songs), chart editing, song creation, JSON/text importing, and cloud backup require free Beta sign-up.
- **Email Sign In & Sign Up**: Create or log into an account using email and password. Includes password recovery ("Forgot password?").
- **User Handles & Profiles**: Set up a unique username handle (e.g. `@jazzbassist`) in the User Menu for direct tune sharing and user discovery.
- **Cloud Library Sync**: Automatically syncs user compositions, catalog standard edits, performance arrangements, and custom settings across all your devices in real time.
- **Give Feedback**: Click "Give Feedback" in the User Menu to open a sleek feedback modal. Submit bug reports, feature requests, sound quality feedback, or general comments with optional contact email and interactive star ratings.
- **Preferences Overview**: Displays current drum kit selection, humanization toggle status, and swing ratio.

### User Tunes, Fork-on-Edit & Tune Sharing
- **User Tunes Collection**: Personal original compositions (`source: 'user'`), imported lead sheets, and custom versions live in the dedicated **User Tunes** collection tab in the Library.
- **Fork-on-Edit**: Modifying any built-in catalog standard automatically creates a personal user fork, keeping the original catalog standard pristine.
- **Tune Sharing**: Click the **Share** button on any active tune to send directly to a user's `@handle`, copy a shareable link (`#share=code`), or display a scannable QR code. Incoming shares land in your top-bar **Inbox**.
- **IP Safety Enforcement**: User-original compositions retain custom lyrics and melody annotations. Catalog standards automatically strip all lyrics and melody data before generating share payloads.

### Bandstand Stage
The animated band graphic above the transport has one icon button in its top-right corner:
- **Expand** — Screen Theater Mode: the stage fills the screen. Esc or the compress button returns to normal.

The hotspot labels (bassist, bass sound, drummer, room, comping style, audience) show on their own and come back whenever you hover the stage; click one to cycle that setting.

### Performance Panel
Directly below the transport. **Use plan**, **Reroll Session**, and **Save default / Reset** sit at the top and apply everywhere; the rest is split into four tabs so you only see what you're working on.

| Tab | What's in it |
| --- | --- |
| **Structure** | The chorus plan — head choruses, how many soloists and how many choruses each, bass/piano features, trading, last head. Plus **Ramp solo intensity** and **Choruses to full**, with a preview of the energy the band will play each chorus (`1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → …`). |
| **Rhythm** | What the band plays: dropdown feel pickers for **First chorus**, **Solo choruses**, and **Out-head**, plus per-section feels under **First chorus sections** and per-section style overrides under **Remaining chorus sections**. |
| **Intro & Ending** | The intro and ending style pickers, including **Tonic Splash** — land on the tonic and mark it with a single cymbal splash, no tag and no held chord. |
| **Arrangements** | Save the whole plan (structure, feels, tempo, rhythm style, solo rhythm) under a name, and load it back later. |

---

## 2. Chord Chart Views

Jam-a-Lot offers multiple layout modes to suit your practicing style:
- **Standard Grid**: A classic 4-column layout mapping bars evenly.
- **Compact View**: An authentic real-book lead sheet style notation that replaces boxy grid lines with thin, traditional bar markings and section dividers.
- **Repeat View**: Collapses repeating sections using standard musical repeat brackets (e.g., `|:` and `:|`). Active bar highlighting is mapped to the first occurrence of repeating sections so your eyes stay aligned with the chart.
- **Vintage View**: The same chords in an amber, terminal-style monospace layout — full form written out, no repeat folding.

---

## 3. Instrument Mixer & Quick Controls

Directly below the chord chart, you can adjust levels and sounds on the fly.
All three instruments play at a calibrated level in decibels (`dB`), where `0.0 dB` represents unity.

### Panning Positions
- Piano: `L35`
- Bass: `R35`
- Kick / Snare: `C / L3`
- Hi-hat / Ride: `L32 / R30`
- Toms: `R18`
- Crash / Splash: `L42 / R38`

### Per-style mixer memory
Faders are remembered per rhythm style as well as per drum kit: each style's band balance comes back when you return to it, an unadjusted style keeps the current faders, and Reset mixer clears them all.

### Mix & EQ Studio
Instrument FX adds separate bass/drums racks: drive with clean blend, low-pass, auto-wah, chorus, phaser, modulation rate, delay/time/feedback and output trim. Both start clean, have independent bypass/reset and persist globally in local audio preferences. Nordic Bass, Drum Echo and Floating Space are creative presets inspired by e.s.t., not exact artist patches. Effects reach room sends, recordings and the listening reference; bypass also mutes delay tails. Chorus/phaser are creative additions.

Toolbox → Mix & EQ Studio opens a panel below the chart that stays open until closed: live RTA spectrum or waterfall spectrogram with Peak/RMS/Crest meters, draggable 6-band EQ with scroll bandwidth and rotary knobs, a Linear preset (adjustable exponent, default Kolmogorov -5/3, approximately -5.02 dB/octave) with automatic level matching, stable zero slope, shortcut buttons for -1, -1/2, 0, +1/2 and +1, and spectrum-aligned overlay, bus levels/pan with a glue compressor, and DJ filter/echo/stutter tools activated on tab selection, with six performance controls above the knobs. Spain merges into Punchy Funk & Groove; legacy textures are retired, and a session-only Mono Check.

---

## 4. The Listening Band
Open **Listening** in the header row to arm the microphone. The band listens in real time and adapts to your performance using frequency-bin audio subtraction.

### Automatic trio balance
All three built-in bass sounds and four comping sounds use phrase-level matching and sound-specific tone shaping across rhythm styles. The nylon guitar receives subsonic cleanup and pluck presence. Reviewed drum and Latin balances are retained, and mixer faders and master EQ stay adjustable.

Desktop Toolbox: vertical toolbar centered at the left edge with all available tool icons, descriptive tooltips, piano keys for Keyboard and an EQ-curve icon distinct from Mixer; up to 1100 px retains the header menu. Hidden in full-screen performance. Neutral beta/guest styling. Instrument FX: Preset defaults to the second entry, Nordic Bass, while staying bypassed until enabled. Off racks collapse. Reset preset restores selected factory defaults or a saved snapshot, double-click restores one knob’s preset value, selected identity persists across edits/reloads, edits are marked, and New preset saves named current-rack snapshots in this browser, separately for bass and drums.
